citation: MIP-9, section 1 (docs/mip/0009-group-conversation.md): messages to the human stand out, a run of messages that woke nobody but agents folds into one line, a line marks where unread messages begin, joins, leaves, pauses and policy changes are merged one-line rows, @muster's messages take no Reply, a body over 40 lines shows its first 40, and dividers are dated yyyy-mm-dd. Folding only runs of two or more, a membership row or a new day ending a run, and judging a policy-woken message by the group's current policy are the implementation's own reading.
why: The thread is what lets the human find the two messages that were for them without reading the other forty. A message for the human folded away, an unread line in the wrong place, or a Reply offered to Muster each fails quietly: nothing crashes, and the human misses a question or answers nobody.

cases.name: the header names the machine keeping a group copied from another
cases.why: A group kept on a devenv says so, since a post there is refused while that machine cannot be reached.

cases.name: a pair group with the human is kept here, whatever its @
cases.why: Every agent-to-human pair group is named @human+agent, and reading the @ in it as a machine would name a machine called human+agent in the header of the most common group there is.

cases.name: a pair group kept on another machine names that machine
cases.why: The last @ names the machine only when something comes before it.

cases.name: a run of messages between agents folds into one line
cases.why: This is the whole point of the thread over the transcript: traffic between agents is out of the way until the human chooses to open it.

cases.name: a lone message between agents is shown rather than folded
cases.why: A fold that hides one message costs the human a click to read the same single line it replaced.

cases.name: a message to the human ends a run and stands out
cases.why: A question for the human folded among agents' chatter is a question the human never sees.

cases.name: an unaddressed message that woke the human through the policy does not fold
cases.why: MIP-9: a message that woke the human through its group's policy, without naming them, was for them as much as one that named them.

cases.name: an unaddressed message in a group that rings every agent folds
cases.why: A ring of * is every member but the human, who is woken only by being named, so such a message woke nobody but agents.

cases.name: an opened fold shows its messages, and stays open as the run grows
cases.why: A fold is named by its first message, so a message arriving at the end of an open run does not close it under the human reading it.

cases.name: Muster's messages are rows of their own with no Reply
cases.why: @muster is never an addressee, so a Reply to it could only be refused; and its notices are about the group, so they do not fold among agents' messages.

cases.name: the human's own messages are shown, named you, with no Reply
cases.why: What the human wrote is part of the conversation they are following, and replying to oneself addresses nobody.

cases.name: an author who left takes no Reply
cases.why: A post to somebody no longer in the group is refused, so offering Reply would lead the human straight into a refusal.

cases.name: a pane participant is named by its callsign and carries its pane
cases.why: A participant's name is its pane id, which says nothing to a person; Go to pane needs the pane the member is in.

cases.name: consecutive joins, leaves and changes merge into one row
cases.why: A group's first minutes are a burst of joins; one line each pushes the first real message off the screen.

rows.members: otter made the group; otter, heron, lynx and you joined; heron paused it

cases.name: the unread line comes before the first message that waited
cases.why: The conversation opens scrolled to where the human stopped reading; a line in the wrong place hides a question above it or makes them reread what they saw.

cases.name: the unread line ends a run so the fold does not swallow it
cases.why: A line inside a folded run would be invisible, and the human would not know where their unread messages begin.

cases.name: a divider starts each day, in the window's own time zone
cases.why: Dates on the dividers are the human's dates: a message at 23:30 UTC belongs to the next day an hour east.

cases.name: a body over 40 lines shows its first 40, and all of it once asked
cases.why: A body runs to 1 MiB; drawing it whole would bury the thread under one message. Show all is per message, and asking for it must show the rest.
